nodes.description: Public dynamic array LoveBlock[] locks storing all love blocks; its length is the total count.
Private mapping(uint => address) lockToOwner recording the creator of each love block id.
Private mapping(address => uint) ownerToNumber counting how many blocks each owner has created.
External function that pushes a new LoveBlock using the caller-supplied message/flag and the current block.timestamp, updates ownership mappings and emits NewLoveBlock.
External view function that iterates over all locks and returns the ids owned by the caller.
Internal pure library function performing checked uint256 addition with an assert.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership writes and lookups.
Miner-influenced block timestamp read as 'now' when creating and emitting a love block.
Counter increment via SafeMath.add(1) on ownerToNumber[msg.sender] and on the local counter; the only arithmetic on user-influenced state.
Storage/event write embedding the current block.timestamp into the LoveBlock struct and the NewLoveBlock event.
String parameter _message supplied by the caller to createLoveBlock.
Bool parameter _encrypted supplied by the caller to createLoveBlock.
Local variable id holding the index returned by locks.push(...) minus 1.
Local memory array result collecting the caller's love block ids.
Local loop counter for the result array, incremented through SafeMath.add.
Local loop index iterating over locks.length in myLoveBlocks.
Local variable c inside SafeMath.add holding the raw sum a + b.

edges.reason: msg.sender is consumed by createLoveBlock without any access-control restriction, allowing any caller to mint an owned block.
Caller address is written into lockToOwner[id], so ownership state is fully caller-controlled.
Caller address indexes ownerToNumber for the increment, so the counter key is attacker-chosen.
block.timestamp (now) is read inside createLoveBlock to stamp the new block, creating timestamp dependency.
The miner-influenced timestamp flows into the persisted timestamps and the emitted event.
User-supplied _message is stored in the new LoveBlock struct.
User-supplied _encrypted flag is stored in the new LoveBlock struct.
Local id derived from locks.push is used as the key to write lockToOwner.
ownerToNumber[msg.sender] is read and passed into the SafeMath.add call site.
The incremented value returns from SafeMath.add and is written back into ownerToNumber.
createLoveBlock unconditionally executes the counter increment operation.
createLoveBlock unconditionally performs the timestamp-dependent struct push and event emit.
SafeMath.add computes a + b into the local c, the unchecked sum.
The asserted local c is returned by SafeMath.add as the checked result.
myLoveBlocks sizes its result array and compares against lockToOwner using the caller address.
ownerToNumber[msg.sender] determines the length of the result array in myLoveBlocks.
The owner's block count sizes the freshly allocated local result array.
lockToOwner[i] is read during the loop to decide whether a block belongs to the caller.
Loop index i drives the indexing of the lockToOwner mapping.
myLoveBlocks iterates its loop index i over locks.length.
Local result array is returned as the function output.
The local counter is passed into the SafeMath.add(1) call inside the loop.
The incremented value is assigned back to the local counter.
locks.length bounds the iteration inside myLoveBlocks.
locks.length is returned directly by totalLoveBlocks.
myLoveBlockCount returns state keyed by the caller-controlled msg.sender.
ownerToNumber is the storage read backing the count returned by myLoveBlockCount.

normalization_plan.reason: The _message parameter has no independent behaviour; it is only consumed by createLoveBlock for struct storage.
The _encrypted parameter is only consumed by createLoveBlock and carries no standalone semantics.
Local id is a transient index produced inside createLoveBlock and does not need separate tracking.
Local result is the return buffer of myLoveBlocks and is fully determined by that function.
Local counter exists only to feed the SafeMath.add increment operation and is subsumed by the arithmetic operation node.
Loop index i is purely a control artifact of myLoveBlocks' iteration.
Local c is the internal sum of SafeMath.add and collapses into that function.
